argument_markdown:
## Source-backed input

Packet artifact C66-001-v3, source SRC-0004, gives the fibrewise obstruction decomposition
H^0(C,omega_C⊗W^vee(Gamma))=H^0(C,omega_C⊗W_4^vee(Gamma))⊕H^0(C,omega_C⊗W_5^vee(Gamma))
and the convention-compatible degree formula deg(W_f)=4g+12-4f. The packet fixes W_5=(O_{P(E^vee)}(2)⊗gamma^*O(-5))|_C, rather than the O(5) summand of F. TASK.json has no dependency artifacts, so no absent dependency is inferred or strengthened.

## Proved steps

For g=6, deg(W_4)=20, deg(W_5)=16, and deg(omega_C)=10. If Gamma has degree six, then

deg(omega_C⊗W_4^vee(Gamma))=10-20+6=-4,

deg(omega_C⊗W_5^vee(Gamma))=10-16+6=0.

The first line bundle has no nonzero section. A degree-zero line bundle on a smooth projective connected curve has a nonzero section exactly when it is trivial: the zero divisor of such a section is effective of degree zero, hence empty. Consequently the entire CE obstruction is nonzero exactly when

omega_C⊗W_5^vee⊗O_C(Gamma)≅O_C,

which is equivalent to O_C(Gamma)≅L:=W_5⊗omega_C^{-1}. Thus Z_ev and the Abel–Jacobi incidence I have the same geometric points. Both are finite-type locally closed substacks over C, so their underlying reduced substacks agree. This conclusion does not compare their nilpotents or multiplicities.

The incidence is constructed without using Proj(pi_*L): it is the base change of the relative Abel–Jacobi map Sym_B^6(C)→Pic^6(C/B) along the section [L]. Its reduced-support part is open. The standard ordering map from six pairwise-distinct sections to their effective divisor is finite étale with free deck group S_6; base change to the Abel–Jacobi fibre gives the asserted torsor.

Finally deg(L)=16-10=6, so on every geometric genus-6 fibre Riemann–Roch gives chi(L)=6-6+1=1 and h^0(L)=1+h^1(L)≥1. Hence the full Abel–Jacobi fibre in Sym^6 is nonempty. This does not imply the existence of a divisor with six distinct points.

## Computational hypotheses

None. No finite experiment is used.

## Gaps and exact-target boundary

The argument does not compare the nonreduced determinantal/Fitting ideal with the Abel–Jacobi ideal, descend W_5 through families lacking a chosen splitting, prove that every fibre contains a reduced divisor, extend across unbalanced or nonreduced strata, or determine components, dimensions, stabilizers, and closure in M_{6,6}. It proves no Tate-type or survival statement for W_{-16}H_16^{BM}(M_{6,6};Q).

## Failed routes

The blocked routes vcd-only-vanishing, undecorated-cgp-top-weight-graph-complex, point-count-without-degree-parity-separation, and forgetful-map-renaming-local-system-unknown are not used. They do not construct the assigned CE evaluation-failure locus, and no new admitted evidence reopens them.

claims.statement: For the balanced CE summands, the obstruction splits into the f=4 and f=5 spaces and deg(W_f)=4g+12-4f with the twist gamma^*O(-f).
At g=n=6 the f=4 obstruction line bundle has degree -4 and the f=5 obstruction line bundle has degree zero.
On every geometric split balanced fibre, CE evaluation fails at Gamma exactly when O_C(Gamma)≅W_5⊗omega_C^{-1}.
The reduced CE failure substack equals the reduced Abel–Jacobi incidence substack, and ordering the reduced support gives a finite étale S_6-torsor.
The full effective-divisor incidence fibre is nonempty on every geometric fibre because deg(L)=6 and chi(L)=1.

No descent of W_5 or L from a chosen split CE base to the unsplit balanced tetragonal moduli stack.

summary: The balanced six-point CE failure locus is rigorously identified, after reduction and on a split balanced base, with the Abel–Jacobi incidence for L=W_5⊗omega^{-1}. The ordered distinct locus is the finite étale S_6-cover of the reduced-support open. This proves a fibrewise/relative reduced construction of Z but not its nonreduced scheme structure, descent to the unsplit balanced stack, or the exact Tate target.

theorem_scope.geometry: smooth tetragonal families with a chosen balanced CE splitting F=O(4)⊕O(5)
theorem_scope.scheme_scope: equality after reduction; no comparison of nonreduced Fitting ideals

theorem_statement: Let B be a finite-type complex base carrying a smooth family of genus-6 tetragonal covers together with an actual balanced Casnati–Ekedahl splitting F=O(4)⊕O(5). Put W_f=(O_{P(E^vee)}(2)⊗gamma^*O(-f))|_C and L=W_5⊗omega_{C/B}^{-1}. On the relative ordered configuration stack Conf_6(C/B), let Z_ev be the Casnati–Ekedahl evaluation-rank-failure locus, and let I be the Abel–Jacobi incidence locus O_C(p_1+⋯+p_6)≅L. Then (Z_ev)_red=I_red. Moreover, the quotient of I_red by S_6 is the reduced-support open of the relative Abel–Jacobi fibre Sym_B^6(C)×_{Pic^6(C/B),[L]}B, and the ordering map is a finite étale S_6-torsor. Every geometric fibre of the full Abel–Jacobi fibre is nonempty, although this theorem does not assert that its reduced-support open is nonempty.
